items.title: Five takeaways from the surprising Mississauga mayoral race
items.summary: The Mississauga mayoral election saw underdog Alvin Tedjo decisively beat two political heavyweights. Alvin Tedjo is swarmed by supporters after he becomes the new mayor for Mississauga. The Mississauga mayoral election was a roller-coaster ride that ended with a shocking underdog win by rookie councillor Alvin Tedjo. His victory over incumbent mayor Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie was also remarkable in that it came with a decisive lead of more than 20,000 votes over Parrish and 30,000 over Crombie with almost all polls reporting. “The polls really underestimated us, but we really smacked them,” said elated Tedjo supporter and University of Toronto Mississauga student Jan Durkiewicz on Monday night. Tedjo, 43, said his win shows that people in Mississauga were ready for someone new. He is the first mayor since 1978 not to be, or have served under the legendary Hazel McCallion. “People in this city are choosing change … and we’re going to deliver that,” Tedjo told reporters. ” Tedjo will now lead a council that he was first elected to four years ago, and will have to deliver on his pledge to freeze the city portion of property taxes for the next two years.

items.title: Every Returning Councillor Who Ran Again Kept Their Seat as Mississauga Picked a New Mayor
items.summary: Insauga.com reports that while Mississauga voters chose change at the mayor's office, they kept every sitting city councillor who sought another term. According to the outlet, the only new faces on council when it convenes in mid-November will fill the wards 2 and 7 seats vacated by Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, both of whom ran for mayor instead. The outlet reports Tedjo's winning tally reached 74,479 votes, ahead of incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish's 51,853 and former mayor Bonnie Crombie's 43,191, while Damerla finished fourth with 11,500 votes. According to insauga.com, ten other mayoral candidates also appeared on the ballot but drew far fewer votes than the top four finishers. The outlet reports the City of Mississauga said late Monday night that all polls had reported, though the results remain unofficial pending further confirmation.

items.title: Tedjo knocks off two political heavyweights to become mayor of Mississauga
items.summary: Back in August, Alvin Tedjo wasn’t given much of a chance as the mayoral race in Mississauga kicked into gear. Tonight, he’s preparing to move into the mayor’s office in the next few weeks after decisively defeating political heavyweights Carolyn Parrish (current Mississauga mayor) and Bonnie Crombie (former mayor) following a hotly contested 2026 Mississauga mayoral campaign. m. ” But “today, the city of Mississauga has made a clear and historic choice to demand a change at city hall,” Tedjo continued, adding “beyond a doubt this is the honour of a lifetime to stand here as your next mayor” of Mississauga. ” Fierce political rivals Parrish and Crombie, identified by pundits early in the race as the presumptive favourites, launched numerous pointed attacks at one another during high-stakes debates and via social media as the campaign progressed. Tedjo, who served as Mississauga Ward 2 councillor the past four years, for the most part steered clear of the main battle and forged his own path forward — culminating in tonight’s win.

Mississauga has elected Alvin Tedjo as the next mayor of the city, capping off a high-stakes race to lead Ontario’s fourth largest city. According to City of Mississauga results, Tedjo secured majority votes over challengers incumbent Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie. 79 per cent of polls reporting, Tedjo captured 71,998 votes, holding off Parrish who placed second with 50,097 votes. “People in this city are choosing change, have chosen change and we’re going to deliver that, Tedjo said addressing his supporters at Wildflower Event Space.

items.title: Who is Alvin Tedjo? 4 things to know about the winner of Mississauga’s mayoral race
items.summary: He was a first-term councillor and a long-shot candidate. From high school student council to an unlikely win, here’s what to know about Alvin Tedjo. Alvin Tedjo, a first-term councillor, has been elected mayor of Mississauga. He grew up with a view of City Hall outside his house. Now, he will be Mississauga’s mayor. Alvin Tedjo, a first-term councillor and former provincial political staffer, staged an unlikely campaign against two titans of Mississauga politics — former mayor Bonnie Crombie and incumbent Carolyn Parrish — to ride to victory on Monday. Here are four things to know about Tedjo. Tedjo’s Chinese-Indonesian parents settled in Mississauga when he was four and he grew up downtown, where he could see City Hall from outside his house. “I saw a lot of the challenges and hardships that come with that immigrant experience,” he said on a 2025 podcast. “If you see something wrong, do something about it,” he said his parents taught him. He was student council president in high school and served on the mayor’s youth advisory committee. He met then-mayor Hazel McCallion in the mid-1990s, when he won an award for being Young Citizen of the Year. “Get into politics, young man,” she told him, he said.

Alvin Tedjo may have started the Mississauga mayoral election as an underdog, but he has managed to beat out former mayor Bonnie Crombie and incumbent Carolyn Parrish to take over the city’s top job, CityNews projects. He won handidly, leading Parrish in second by over 20,000 votes, despite early polls showing a tight race leading up to election. “Our optimism, our hope, our vision for what this city could be, our positivity and our unstoppable effort to reach every single resident in the city of Mississauga, to put forward practical solutions that would make a difference in their lives and to earn their trust, all of that hard work has led us to this moment,” said Tedjo in his victory speech.

items.title: Rookie Councillor's Six-Month Climb From Fourth Place Ends in Mississauga's Top Job
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports Alvin Tedjo, a first-term city councillor, has won Mississauga's mayoral race after his campaign started in a distant fourth place six months ago. According to the newspaper, the 43-year-old overtook incumbent Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor, former mayor and Ontario Liberal leader Bonnie Crombie, who had held a narrow lead in polling heading into election day. The Star reports that with 89 per cent of polls reporting on election night, Tedjo led by more than 18,000 votes. At his victory party, Tedjo told cheering supporters that Mississauga had voted for change, and said that when his team started out, people had told them they could not win. According to the outlet, Crombie called Tedjo to congratulate him and, standing on stage with her three children, said his energy and enthusiasm had inspired people to believe they could help shape the city's future.

items.title: Party Turns Deadly in Mississauga Industrial Lot, Ending in a Brampton Man's Murder Charge
items.summary: The Toronto Star reports that Kevin Chippie, a 35-year-old man from Brampton, turned himself in to Peel police less than two hours after investigators publicly identified him as a suspect in a fatal stabbing. According to the newspaper, the stabbing happened early Sunday in the parking lot of an industrial area near Tomken Road and Kamato Road, where officers found a man with life-threatening injuries who was later pronounced dead at the scene. The Star reports police believe a party had been underway in the area and that both the suspect and the victim had been attending it. Investigators told the outlet the stabbing was an isolated incident and that there was no ongoing threat to public safety. According to the Star, Chippie was arrested and charged with second-degree murder once he surrendered to homicide detectives on Monday.

items.title: What residents should know as they vote on election day in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga residents are casting their ballots today and this evening following months of campaigning by candidates running for mayor, city council and school board trustee positions. Headlining the 2026 municipal election in Mississauga is a hotly contested mayoral race featuring four main candidates — including the current mayor and her predecessor — among a larger field of 14 hopefuls vying for the city’s top elected office. Incumbent Carolyn Parrish and former mayor Bonnie Crombie, who traded pointed attacks during the campaign’s high-stakes debates, are attempting to fend off challenges from city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla. Campaign watchers in Mississauga — and several polls — note more recently Tedjo appears to have garnered additional support that has perhaps vaulted him into a close three-way race as election night arrives. Record numbers turned out for advance voting Municipal election voters who didn’t cast ballots earlier this month during record-setting advance polling in Mississauga are doing so today and tonight. m. across the city. The victorious candidates will serve in their positions for the next term of office, which runs from 2026-2030.
